title: Policy Analysis Dashboard — AI Output Schema
description: Canonical schema for AI-generated outcome domain JSON files. Files matching this schema are written to chatgpt_responses/{outcome_id}.json and loaded by the dashboard UI. The top-level key names ('Legal Standards', 'Tiers', 'Governing Agencies') must be preserved exactly as shown — the UI reads them by these exact strings.

meta.description: Outcome-level metadata injected from the static config. Not rendered directly by the UI but used for traceability.

outcome_domain.description: Snake-case identifier matching the config outcome.domain_label.

tier_interpretation_note.description: Plain-language note explaining how tiers should be interpreted for this outcome domain.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp set by the pipeline at generation time.

config_version.description: Semver string of the config file used to generate this output.

Legal Standards.description: One object per legal standard relevant to this outcome domain. The legal_standard_id is the backbone — every policy in Tiers and every agency in Governing Agencies references these IDs.

legal_standard_id.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE identifier. Must match a canonical ID from the config's legal_standards.standards array. Never invent new IDs; use only what the config defines.

legal_standard.description: Full formal name of the legal standard, including citation in parentheses where appropriate.

caption.description: One-sentence plain-language summary shown as a subtitle on the legal standard card in the UI.

info.description: Full explanatory paragraph(s) shown in the expanded card body. Should explain the mechanism by which this standard affects the outcome domain.

vocabulary.description: Key terms and definitions for this legal standard. May be empty array if no terms are needed.

sources.description: List of authoritative source strings (statute citations, agency document titles, etc.) supporting this legal standard entry.

order.description: Optional. When present, the UI draws a visual connector pairing the legal standard with the manual-side card that shares the same order value. Used for cross-panel comparison alignment.

Tiers.description: One key per tier (Tier 1 through Tier 4). Each contains the threshold label and an array of policy entries that are 'in play' when the outcome is in that tier.

Governing Agencies.description: Agencies with authority over legal standards relevant to this outcome domain. Sorted by the UI in descending order of pertains_to_legal_standards array length.

name.description: Full agency name with abbreviation in parentheses.

note.description: Plain-language description of the agency's role with respect to this outcome domain. Should reference specific legal standards by name.

pertains_to_legal_standards.description: Array of legal_standard_id strings this agency governs. Must reference only canonical IDs defined in the Legal Standards array above.

threshold.description: Short label describing the outcome condition for this tier (e.g., 'Revenue declining <5%/year'). Must match the value defined in the config tiers array.

policies.description: Legal standards that are active, implicated, or in play when the outcome is in this tier. May be empty if no standards are meaningfully applicable.

policy_name.description: Short display name for the policy entry shown on the policy card. May abbreviate the full legal standard name.

legal_standard_id.description: Must reference a canonical legal_standard_id from the Legal Standards array in this file.

relationship.description: Display label shown on the policy card by the current UI. Must mirror effect_type in human-readable form: 'Direct' when effect_type is 'direct', 'Indirect' when effect_type is 'indirect'. Kept as a separate field for UI compatibility; the canonical machine-readable classification lives in effect_type.

effect_type.description: Canonical machine-readable classification. 'direct' = clear operational or regulatory pathway affecting conditions relevant to this tier. 'indirect' = conditional, secondary, or system-level influence. Drives the value of relationship and any future UI logic.

note.description: Explanatory note shown in the expanded policy card Details section. Should describe the mechanism (how this standard drives the tier condition).
